prompt: A stadium has 60,000 seats and orders average four seats each. What does this imply for an on-sale with two million shoppers?

options.text: Only about 15,000 complete orders can succeed under that average
options.explanation: Correct. Divide the sixty thousand seats into groups of four. Fifteen thousand orders exhaust supply under the assumed average, so admission fairness and inexpensive waiting matter more than admitting the whole crowd.

options.text: All two million shoppers should reach the inventory database immediately
options.explanation: Wrong. Admitting the whole crowd overloads the core without increasing supply.

options.text: The event can satisfy about 500,000 complete four-seat orders
options.explanation: Wrong. Five hundred thousand groups of four exceed the available seats.

options.text: A faster seat-map cache creates more available seats
options.explanation: Wrong. Faster cached views do not create inventory.

workedExample:
```formula
O = S / q
O = 60,000 / 4 = 15,000
where
O: successful orders under the stated average
S: available seats; here 60,000
q: average seats bought per order; here 4
In words: The stadium supplies fifteen thousand average four-seat orders; admitting more shoppers does not create inventory.
```
